title: Helm: optionally deploy scheduled backup CronJob for Redwood Private control plane
creator: Ethan Park
project: Private Day-2 Ops: Backup/Restore + DR Toolkit
description:
Goal
Add an optional scheduled backup CronJob to the Redwood Private Helm charts so customers can run consistent, repeatable control-plane backups without hand-rolling Kubernetes YAML. The CronJob must be configurable for constrained environments (restricted IAM/egress, air-gapped), must not require storing plaintext secrets in the cluster beyond what Private already requires, and must provide sane defaults for retries/resource limits.

Scope
- Helm values + templates to deploy a Kubernetes CronJob that runs `redwood-private-installer backup create` (or the chart-provided wrapper entrypoint) on a schedule.
- RBAC + ServiceAccount for the backup job with least privilege.
- Resource requests/limits, retry policy, job history limits, concurrency policy.
- Secrets handling: read backup config from existing Kubernetes Secrets/ConfigMaps and/or env vars; do not template secret material into rendered manifests.
- Optional integration points for backup storage backends (S3+KMS, NFS) by passing configuration references through env/volume mounts.

Non-goals
- Implementing the backup logic itself (tracked in ENG-9821).
- Terraform provisioning for buckets/keys/IAM (ENG-9825).
- Restore Job hooks (separate ticket/PR line; see ENG-9822 and helm PR plan).

Background / Why
Multiple enterprise Private accounts asked for a supported ‘set-and-forget’ backup mechanism. Today we have ad-hoc scripts that are easy to misconfigure (RBAC issues, missing env vars, resource starvation). A chart-native CronJob gives a consistent and supportable deployment surface and allows us to standardize observability signals.

Requirements / Acceptance Criteria
1) Values-driven enablement
- Default: disabled.
- Values keys (proposed):
  - `backupCronjob.enabled` (bool)
  - `backupCronjob.schedule` (cron string)
  - `backupCronjob.suspend` (bool)
  - `backupCronjob.concurrencyPolicy` (Forbid by default)
  - `backupCronjob.startingDeadlineSeconds` (optional)
  - `backupCronjob.successfulJobsHistoryLimit` / `backupCronjob.failedJobsHistoryLimit`
  - `backupCronjob.backoffLimit` (default 3)
  - `backupCronjob.activeDeadlineSeconds` (optional)
  - `backupCronjob.resources.requests/limits` (CPU/mem)
  - `backupCronjob.nodeSelector/tolerations/affinity` passthrough
  - `backupCronjob.extraEnv` and `backupCronjob.envFromSecretRefs` (string refs only)

2) RBAC + ServiceAccount
- CronJob runs under a dedicated ServiceAccount.
- Minimum required permissions:
  - Read-only access to namespaces/resources needed to capture deployment config that is in-scope (e.g., reading specific ConfigMaps/Secrets references if required by backup manifest generation).
  - If the backup tool needs to query cluster objects for inventory, ensure it only has `get/list` on the specific API groups/resources; avoid wildcard `*`.
- No cluster-admin requirement.

3) Secrets handling / Security
- Do not render secret values from `values.yaml` directly into manifests.
- Support referencing an existing Kubernetes Secret (e.g., `backupCronjob.envFromSecretRefs: ["redwood-backup-config"]`).
- If credentials are needed for object storage, they must come from:
  - cloud-native identity (IRSA / workload identity) where available, OR
  - a customer-managed Secret reference that the job mounts/reads.
- If encryption is enabled (KMS envelope encryption), the CronJob must pass only key identifiers / endpoints (not key material) via env/args.
- Add documentation notes in chart README: recommended patterns for S3+KMS (IRSA) and NFS (no_root_squash discouraged; permission guardrails).

4) Operational defaults
- Use `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` by default to prevent overlapping backups.
- Set a default `backoffLimit` and clearly document the retry semantics.
- Provide default resource requests/limits that won’t starve the cluster but also won’t OOM on mid-size control planes (initial proposal: requests 250m CPU / 512Mi; limits 1 CPU / 2Gi; final numbers TBD after staging runs).
- Provide a mechanism to tune timeout (`activeDeadlineSeconds`) in slow object stores.

5) Observability hooks
- Ensure the job logs are structured and include a summary line with: backup_id, artifact_manifest_path, bytes_written, duration_seconds, status.
- Include labels/annotations on the job/pod to allow scraping and dashboards (ties into ENG-9826 metrics).

6) Upgrade safety
- Enabling/disabling the CronJob should not impact existing deployments.
- Chart changes must be backwards compatible with existing values files.

Implementation Notes (proposed)
- Template files:
  - `templates/backup-cronjob.yaml` (CronJob + Job spec)
  - `templates/backup-serviceaccount.yaml`
  - `templates/backup-role.yaml` and `templates/backup-rolebinding.yaml`
- Command pattern:
  - Use the same container image as the control-plane utility image OR a dedicated ‘tools’ image referenced by the chart.
  - Entrypoint example:
    - `redwood-private-installer backup create --output=<path> --storage-config=<mounted path> --encryption-config=<mounted path>`
  - Write temp artifacts to an emptyDir, then upload to configured backend.

Testing Plan
- Helm unit/lint:
  - `helm template` with `backupCronjob.enabled=true` produces CronJob + RBAC + SA.
  - `helm template` with `enabled=false` produces no backup resources.
- Staging validation:
  - Enable CronJob on staging Private cluster (VPC) with S3 backend.
  - Verify:
    - Cron schedule triggers
    - No RBAC errors
    - Backup artifacts are encrypted at rest and manifest is written
    - Job retries behave as expected on transient failures
- Air-gapped validation (best-effort):
  - Validate chart can deploy without pulling external charts/images beyond what the on-prem bundle provides (coordinate with release packaging work).

Open Questions
- Do we need to include any Kubernetes object capture (e.g., Helm release values) as part of this CronJob, or is it purely invoking the backup CLI which already captures what it needs? (See internal debate; ensure alignment with backup scope in ADR.)
- Should we ship a default schedule (e.g., daily at 02:00) or require explicit schedule when enabled?

Links
- Related tickets: ENG-9821 (backup CLI), ENG-9823 (envelope encryption), ENG-9826 (metrics/alerts)
- Helm PR (planned/active): sources/github/redwood-helm-charts/pr-131-enable-backup-cronjob-values-and-rbac.json
comments: 2025-02-03 (Bruno Silva): Drafted values schema for `backupCronjob.*`. Defaulting `enabled=false`, `concurrencyPolicy=Forbid`, `backoffLimit=3`. Need final resource defaults after one staging run; current guess is requests 250m/512Mi, limits 1CPU/2Gi.

2025-02-05 (Sean Gallagher): Please make sure we can set `startingDeadlineSeconds` and `activeDeadlineSeconds`. We saw slow object storage cause jobs to exceed default kube timeouts in a lab setup. Also +1 on `successfulJobsHistoryLimit` low to reduce noise.

2025-02-06 (Marcus Lin): Hard requirement: no secret material in Helm values that ends up in rendered manifests. Secret refs only. Also ensure RBAC is not wildcarded. If the job needs to read any Secrets, it must be explicitly scoped by name/namespace (or avoid reading secrets entirely and rely on envFrom).

2025-02-10 (Hanae Suzuki): For KMS endpoints/Key IDs: pass as env vars; do not bake into configmap if it includes anything sensitive. Key IDs are OK; key material is not. Ensure the job fails fast with a clear error if KMS is unreachable (don’t silently write unencrypted backups).

2025-02-13 (Bruno Silva): Implemented templates: CronJob + SA + Role/RoleBinding. Role currently allows get/list ConfigMaps in the release namespace for reading non-secret config (needed by backup CLI to find control-plane endpoints). No Secrets access in RBAC. Credentials expected via IRSA or envFrom Secret.

2025-02-17 (Allison Grant): Add standard labels to CronJob/Pods: `app.kubernetes.io/component=backup`, `redwood.ai/operation=backup`. This will simplify dashboards and log routing. Ensure job name includes release name for multi-tenant clusters.

2025-02-20 (Ethan Park): Marking In Review. Please double-check that enabling the CronJob does not restart any existing workloads. Also verify `helm upgrade` doesn’t thrash job history objects. Once merged, coordinate with ENG-9826 so metrics/alerts pick up the new labels.
